teachingPageSubtitle: [Dr. Wang](/team) instructs a range of courses focused on robotics, control, and machine learning. These courses blend theoretical foundations with hands-on applications, preparing students for real-world challenges in robotics design and implementation.

teachings.teachingsData: MECH 4238 is a new undergraduate course in the newly established Mechatronics Stream within the [Department of Mechanical Engineering](https://umanitoba.ca/engineering/faculty-staff/mechanical-engineering). The course introduces the modeling and control of robotic manipulators, starting with kinematics and Jacobian-based velocity and force analysis. Students learn to use analytical mechanics to derive dynamic models of robotic arms and to design and evaluate control laws for multi-degree-of-freedom manipulators. Building on this foundation, the course introduces AI-enhanced control methods, including Gaussian process (GP)-based residual modeling and GP-PID control. By the end of the course, students will understand how physics-based control and data-driven techniques can be combined to achieve accurate and robust control of robotic manipulators. The course was offered in Winter 2026 and will be offered again in **Fall 2026**.

MECH 3550 is a new undergraduate course in the newly established Mechatronics Stream within the [Department of Mechanical Engineering](https://umanitoba.ca/engineering/faculty-staff/mechanical-engineering), offering an *introduction to robotics*. The course covers the fundamental principles of robotic manipulator kinematics, dynamics, and control. Students learn to represent and analyze robot motion, model the forces and torques governing manipulator behavior, and design controllers for accurate and stable performance. Topics include homogeneous transformations, Denavit–Hartenberg (D–H) modeling, forward and inverse kinematics, Jacobian-based velocity and force analysis, singularities, manipulator dynamics, and trajectory tracking through simulation and control design. The course was offered in **Fall 2025**.

This is a new graduate course within the newly established Mechatronics Stream within the [Department of Mechanical Engineering](https://umanitoba.ca/engineering/faculty-staff/mechanical-engineering), covering *advanced topics in mobile robotics*. The course covers AI-enhanced navigation and control for mobile robotic systems, with emphasis on real-world implementation and deployment. The course was offered in Fall 2025 and Winter 2026. It will be offered again in **Winter 2027**.
